biography: David Hart, a name now synonymous with flamboyant speed in the Chevrolet racing circuit, hails from a small, unassuming Dutch village where tulips and windmills were far more common than roaring engines. His infatuation with motorsport began not on the track, but in his grandfather's garage, tinkering with a dilapidated Opel Kadett. He transformed it into a surprisingly competitive autocross machine. A defining moment came at the Zandvoort Circuit during a national amateur race, where, starting from the back of the grid, Hart carved his way through the field with daring overtakes, ultimately clinching victory. This performance caught the eye of a Chevrolet team scout. Now, at 26, Hart is at the peak of his career, a rising star with a reputation for pushing his car and his luck to the absolute limit.
drivingStyle: Hart's driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He's a master of late braking, often diving into corners where others wouldn't dare. He possesses an uncanny ability to find grip where it seemingly doesn't exist. While his tire management isn't always the most delicate, his raw speed and unwavering determination often compensate. Under pressure, Hart thrives, transforming into an even more formidable competitor, relishing the challenge of wheel-to-wheel combat.

famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in the Chevrolet Corvette, showcasing incredible stamina and skill in a grueling endurance race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Daytona 500 due to a mechanical failure, a heartbreaking defeat that cost him a shot at the championship.
